key_insight: Steady incompressible free-boundary flows in an ideal hydromagnetic star can arise as axisymmetric field-aligned or cross-field solutions, with magnetic topology and tangential discontinuities playing a central role.
engineering_relevance: The work clarifies how near-ideal magnetofluid systems can self-organize through reconnection and energy loss, informing models of plasma confinement, stellar dynamics, and solar eruption persistence.
method: Analyzes steady, axisymmetric incompressible MHD flows using the Tsinganos equation.
Treats both classic field-aligned solutions and a new family of cross-field flows.
Separates the strictly ideal limit from near-ideal dissipative behavior to interpret reconnection-driven evolution.
evidence_signal: The paper is a self-contained theoretical study, so its support comes from analytic construction and physical interpretation rather than experimental or simulation datasets.
watch_item: The results rely on idealized assumptions such as incompressibility, axisymmetry, and free-boundary equilibrium, so extension to fully realistic stellar plasmas may require additional physics.
paper_title: The steady incompressible ideal free-boundary flows of a hydromagnetic star
